diff2ai.text: The retry-exhausted delete branch (retryCount > 1) has no method filter, causing the SMS cron job to delete any WorkflowReminder with retryCount exceeding 1, including EMAIL and WHATSAPP reminders

Failure inside the catch block aborts the whole batch - if prisma.workflowReminder.update fails (DB hiccup or concurrent row deletion), the exception escapes the loop, skipping remaining reminders and returning 500 instead of ok: true
Non-atomic increment for retryCount (retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1) uses a stale read value, causing lost increments if two cron invocations overlap
Magic number gt: 1 for retry limit is undocumented and easy to misread - should extract a named constant like MAX_SMS_RETRIES
Failed reminders are hard-deleted with no logging, leaving no trace of why attendees or hosts never received SMS notifications
Unindexed OR predicate with retryCount column and no method filter will force sequential scan of entire WorkflowReminder table on every cron run
The `queued` default value `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, causing all AssignmentSource instances to share the same stale timestamp in long-running processes
`to_dict()` returns a raw datetime for `queued` which fails JSON serialization or becomes a string that violates the type when reconstructed via `from_dict`
The `sync_assignee_outbound` implementations across providers may not accept the new `assignment_source` kwarg, causing TypeError for any provider without `**kwargs` or explicit parameter
The `assignment_source` parameter was incorrectly added to `sync_status_outbound` instead of `sync_assignee_outbound` - no caller passes it to status sync and status sync doesn't use AssignmentSource
Missing test for deassign cycle-breaking when source integration matches target
Missing test for propagation to other integrations when source is from a different integration
Posts with cook_method == raw_html skip sanitization, allowing stored XSS from untrusted RSS/Atom feeds and remote pages containing malicious HTML or javascript: URLs
URL is interpolated directly into href attribute without escaping, allowing attribute breakout with single quotes to inject event handlers
Kernel#open on URL strings allows shell command execution if string starts with pipe character, and import_remote receives untrusted URLs from Disqus exports
Protocol-relative URLs starting with // are incorrectly matched by href.start_with?('/') check, causing them to be mangled into broken URLs
ERB template uses 'end if' which compiles incorrectly, causing rendering to work only by accident with altered output ordering
Feed items without content element cause NoMethodError when calling .scrub on nil, and one bad item aborts processing of entire feed due to retry: false
Every request for unknown embed_url enqueues a job without checking throttle, allowing queue flooding by anonymous visitors with arbitrary embed_url values
Redis throttle using setnx followed by separate expire is not atomic - if process dies between calls, key never expires and URL is permanently blocked
Modifying already-shipped migration create_top_topics has no effect on existing installs, and force: true can silently destroy data
Disqus importer regressed: --category option removed, created_at no longer preserved, and network errors during HTTP fetch abort entire import
If embedded post has been deleted, embed.post is nil and PostRevisor.new(nil).revise! raises, breaking feed polling for all subsequent items
postMessage handler uses indexOf substring check for origin comparison, allowing origins like forum.example.co to pass when expecting forum.example.com
Controller spec expects TopicRetriever.new but controller actually calls Jobs.enqueue, so spec only passes if jobs run inline in test environment
